description: Coverage accounting. 'quarantine' lists tests that no CI leg executes, each with an owner, a review date and the gap it leaves; the Safety evidence job fails on any other never-executed test. 'dispositions' explain removed or weakened coverage; check_coverage_regression.py accepts only dispositions added by the same change. See docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

quarantine.reason: Collation.Default snapshots the culture once per process, so the test passes only as the first LiteDB use in the process; after another test created a database it sees that culture instead of 'fi'.
quarantine.gap: A new database taking its collation from the current thread culture is not asserted on any CI leg; product behaviour (process-wide snapshot) decides whether the test can be made order-independent.

quarantine.reason: Not supported yet: rebuilding 'ana'/'ANA' from en-US/None to en-US/IgnoreCase throws 'Cannot insert duplicate key' instead of recording the collision in _rebuild_errors.
quarantine.gap: Rebuilding to a collation under which unique keys collide is not exercised; the expected _rebuild_errors behaviour is not implemented.

quarantine.reason: Takes ~102 s (100 iterations with a 1 s sleep; passed 5/5 locally on net10.0). The DiskWriterQueue race of #2127 no longer exists; the queue was removed in 198f0a672.
quarantine.gap: Back-to-back file-backed inserts into 100 recreated databases do not run in CI; the original race cannot recur, so the test is a candidate to retire as obsolete.

dispositions.invariant: Every test leg's results are uploaded and judged; no existing timeout, filter or partition changes.
dispositions.reason: Adds the Safety policy and Safety evidence jobs (10-minute limits) and a results upload for the .NET Framework leg, which uploaded nothing before; existing test steps keep their timeouts and filters.

dispositions.invariant: A checkpoint on a log that answers "cannot sync" never loses a commit and never tears the data file; it retries the log sync and drains the WAL once the log syncs.
dispositions.reason: Decision D: no in-place overwrite behind a recovery copy that is only in the OS cache, in both commit modes. Such a checkpoint now writes nothing and keeps the WAL (it used to overwrite data in write order). The new tests assert byte-identical files, kept frames, the drain once the log syncs and power-loss images. (S09a; the durable-commit fail-loud variant follows with S09c.)

dispositions.invariant: Storage that cannot sync never reuses retired WAL slots, and a snapshot checkpoint there keeps the reader's snapshot and every commit.
dispositions.reason: Renamed for the opted-out mode it runs in; a checkpoint whose log cannot sync now retires nothing (it proves its syncs first), so the slot-clear case is forced by a log that stops syncing at the clears.

dispositions.invariant: A shared connection on a log that cannot sync never reuses slots retired there, keeps the reader's snapshot, and a checkpoint whose log cannot sync writes nothing to the data file.
dispositions.reason: Decision D and the retirement proof: a checkpoint on a log known not to sync, or that stops syncing after its proof, now retires and writes nothing; only a log that stops at the sync of the clears leaves cleared slots, which no later engine (of this or another connection) reuses. Asserted per stop point, with a second connection.

dispositions.invariant: A database on a log that never syncs keeps every committed row, and no format change tears its header.
dispositions.reason: Decision D: an index migration, a 5.x conversion or a compact promotion overwrites the header behind a journal the log cannot make durable, so it is refused before it writes, in both commit modes: the open throws the refusal (tagged as unsynced storage) with both files byte for byte, and a compact write stores BSON instead. They used to publish the new format behind an OS-cached journal. The new-database test runs opted out, as the storage requires. (The read-only open fallback after such a refusal follows with S09c.)

dispositions.invariant: An opted-out checkpoint makes the log durable before it overwrites data.
dispositions.reason: The opted-out checkpoint's sync order gained the data sync first (a checkpoint writes only to a data file that just synced), so the test was renamed with the new order and now also checks that no data page is written before the log syncs.

dispositions.invariant: Recovery from an OS-cached promotion journal never replaces a valid header with the journal's copy.
dispositions.reason: e4b9553fd: before the sync that retires a header journal, recovery writes the header back as read (a failed sync's pages may be marked clean, fsyncgate). The recovered-open check was "no data write at all"; it is now "the data file's bytes are unchanged", which still fails if the journal's copy replaced a valid header.
